newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki trims gains, eyes Merita and Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki trims gains, eyes Merita and Wall St.

text.p: Shares ended a lively session higher on Wednesday after trimming gains in late trade as some investors took profits and moved to the sidelines ahead of banking group Merita's earnings report due early on Thursday.
The HEX index rose 0.44 percent to 2,227.23. Volume was a healthy 449 million markka.
Wall Street's full reaction to the U.S. election outcome would set sentiment for the rest of the week, brokers said.
Merita A closed down 0.20 markka at 13.80 -- its first decline since October 29 when it fell 0.50 markka to 13.00.
"Some investors took profits ahead of Merita's results," one broker said, adding that this reversed gains particularly in banking stocks.
The median forecast for Merita's nine-month profit after credit losses is 952 million markka, compared to 482 million in the same period in 1995.
"It depends on Wall Street's reaction to the elections which direction Helsinki will take tomorrow," the broker said.
Telecom heavyweight Nokia was lively and added 2.60 markka to recent gains to close at 215.60. Nokia made up 43 percent of total bourse volume.

Software house TT Tieto extended pre-result gains and rose 6.00 to an all-time high 326.00 markka after reporting a 134 million markka January-September profit -- matching the highest forecast and more than doubling the 65 million in 1995.
Forestry group Metsa-Serla closed up 0.50 at 30.50 after hitting 31.50 on the sale of its chemicals plants for 1.05 billion markka -- a deal which brokers said would boost its balance sheet.
This cast a few beams of light onto the sector's gloomy picture, but brokers could not say whether forestries would resume their recent slide on Thursday.
UPM-Kymmene remained weak and fell 0.60 to a new 87.80 markka record-low close after touching a lowest ever 87.70.
